title: Northwind — Sales Performance
description: Revenue, orders and product mix. Every panel reads the current-row views: ReplacingMergeTree leaves unmerged duplicates behind and SCD type 2 keeps closed rows, both of which would inflate these figures.

list.name: category
list.label: Category
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT category_name FROM v_DimProducts_Current ORDER BY category_name

list.name: country
list.label: Ship country
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM DimGeography FINAL WHERE country != '' ORDER BY country

panels.title: Net revenue
panels.description: Total across the selected period. Sum of line_total — unit_price × quantity × (1 − discount) — materialised at insert so it is computed once rather than on every query. The sparkline underneath is the monthly series the total is drawn from.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMonth(d.full_date) AS time, round(sum(f.line_total), 2) AS revenue FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = f.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' AND g.country LIKE '${country:pipe}' GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Orders
panels.description: Distinct order ids across the period. The fact grain is (order, product), so a row count would count order lines instead.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMonth(d.full_date) AS time, uniqExact(f.order_id) AS orders FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = f.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' AND g.country LIKE '${country:pipe}' GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Average order
panels.description: Revenue per order, aggregating lines to orders first and then averaging the monthly figures. Averaging line_total directly would give the average line, not the average order.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, round(avg(order_total), 2) AS avg_order FROM (SELECT toStartOfMonth(d.full_date) AS time, f.order_id, sum(f.line_total) AS order_total FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = f.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' AND g.country LIKE '${country:pipe}' GROUP BY time, f.order_id) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Fill rate
panels.description: Share of orders that shipped. An unshipped order carries shipped_date_key 0 — the deliberate miss value, not a null.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * uniqExactIf(order_id, shipped_date_key > 0) / uniqExact(order_id), 1) AS shipped_pct FROM v_FactOrders_Current

panels.title: Freight cost
panels.description: Freight belongs to the order but repeats on every line, so it is deduplicated per order before summing. Summing it directly multiplies it by the number of lines per order — the classic fan trap on a master/detail fact.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(sum(freight), 0) AS freight FROM (SELECT DISTINCT order_id, freight FROM v_FactOrders_Current)

panels.title: Revenue and orders over time
panels.description: Revenue on the left axis, order count on the right. Joined to DimDate rather than deriving the month from order_date, so calendar attributes stay defined in one place.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMonth(d.full_date) AS time, round(sum(f.line_total), 0) AS "Revenue", uniqExact(f.order_id) AS "Orders" FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = f.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' AND g.country LIKE '${country:pipe}' GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Revenue by category
panels.description: Category lives on DimProducts rather than in a dimension of its own — the snowflake was flattened during staging.

targets.rawSql: SELECT p.category_name AS category, round(sum(f.line_total), 0) AS revenue FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = f.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' AND g.country LIKE '${country:pipe}' GROUP BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC

SELECT p.product_name AS product, round(sum(f.line_total), 0) AS revenue FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = f.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' AND g.country LIKE '${country:pipe}' GROUP BY product ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Top customers
panels.description: Contact name is carried alongside the company so the table fills the width it is given rather than leaving the right half empty.

targets.rawSql: SELECT c.company_name AS customer, c.contact_name AS contact, g.country AS country, uniqExact(f.order_id) AS orders, round(sum(f.line_total), 2) AS revenue FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN v_DimCustomer_Current AS c ON c.customer_key = f.customer_key INNER JOIN v_DimProducts_Current AS p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN DimGeography AS g ON g.geography_key = c.geography_key WHERE p.category_name LIKE '${category:pipe}' GROUP BY customer, contact, country ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 12

panels.title: Orders by day of week
panels.description: Day names come from DimDate rather than being derived per query, which is the point of having a date dimension. Saturday and Sunday show zero: Northwind's orders were only ever placed on weekdays, and a visible gap says more than a missing bar.

targets.rawSql: SELECT d.day_of_week_name AS day, countIf(f.order_id != 0) AS orders FROM DimDate AS d LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT order_id, order_date_key FROM v_FactOrders_Current) AS f ON f.order_date_key = d.date_key WHERE d.full_date BETWEEN toDate('1996-07-01') AND toDate('1998-05-31') GROUP BY day, d.day_of_week ORDER BY d.day_of_week

panels.title: Revenue by season
panels.description: Labelled with the year because the seasons repeat across the dataset — bare season names would put three winters side by side with no way to tell them apart.

targets.rawSql: SELECT concat(toString(d.calendar_year), ' ', d.season_name) AS period, round(sum(f.line_total), 1) AS revenue FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key GROUP BY period, d.calendar_year, d.calendar_season ORDER BY d.calendar_year, d.calendar_season
SELECT toStartOfMonth(d.full_date) AS time, uniqExact(f.order_id) AS orders FROM v_FactOrders_Current AS f INNER JOIN DimDate AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
